clue.text: Flying body causes delay in match

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is set inside the other here, the delay going into the match

parts.note: a fusee is a kind of windproof match
lag means a delay

explanation.surface: Something holds up the start of a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting fixture but is FUSEE, an old windproof match; LAG goes in after its FUSE, before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of an aircraft, the part that flies, is called this.

clue.text: Life so strangely thread-like

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the two words before it are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Existence is oddly like a fine strand.
explanation.definitionFit: Filose describes something with a slender filament, a fine fibre.

clue.text: Margaret, old-fashioned, not right in a 16

parts.note: square means conventional or old-fashioned
Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: A dated woman named Margaret does not fit in somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is ROUND HOLE, and the saying is that a misfit is a square peg in a round hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit, in the proverb, is a square-shaped plug that will not fit the circular opening.

clue.text: Port the French have round the railhead

parts.note: le is the French for the

indicators.note: round says the word have is placed about the letter for railhead

parts.note: taken as written
the head, or first letter, of rail is R

explanation.surface: A French harbour town surrounds the end of a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major seaport in northern France.

clue.text: Horses go to grass, say

indicators.note: say signals that we want a word with the same spoken form

parts.note: graze means to feed on grass

explanation.surface: Horses are turned out to pasture, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Greys are grey-coated horses.

clue.text: Acadians have no vans without this moulding

indicators.note: without tells us the letters of the following words are taken away from the people named before

parts.note: the Acadians were French settlers of Nova ..., so they are Nova Scotians
the letters N, O, V, A, N, S, removed in that order

explanation.surface: Canadian settlers lack delivery vehicles and so lack a decorative feature.
explanation.walkthrough: Write Acadians as NOVA SCOTIANS, then remove NOVA and the final N and S (the letters of 'no vans', in order) to leave SCOTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scotia is a concave moulding at the base of a classical column.

clue.text: Hearts pilgrims wore on their hats?

explanation.surface: Emblems that devout travellers wore in their caps.
explanation.walkthrough: The cockles of the heart are its depths; pilgrims to Santiago wore scallop shells on their hats.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'warm the cockles of your heart' makes them the innermost feelings; these shellfish shells were pilgrim badges.

clue.text: Tom as a rule is practical

explanation.surface: A man called Tom is usually down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of folk tale; a rule of thumb is a practical guide rather than a precise one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom ___ is the tiny folk-tale hero, and a rule of this kind is a rough practical method.

clue.text: Sad negation of Oedipus's daughter

indicators.note: sad here means in a sorry state, so the letters of negation are disordered

explanation.surface: Oedipus's child gives a mournful refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigone is the daughter of Oedipus in Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Vessel holds the right spirit for a music-maker

indicators.note: holds says the vessel contains the other two pieces

parts.note: a vial is a small vessel for liquid
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A container keeps the proper alcohol for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A virginal is an early keyboard instrument of the harpsichord family.

clue.text: Response in the case of a comic author lecturing

definitions.text: Response in the case of a comic author lecturing

parts.words: Response in the case of a comic author lecturing
parts.note: a case is a legal hearing, and the comic speaker is a witty judge whose jokes draw a reaction noted in the law reports

explanation.surface: An audience reacts when a humorous writer gives a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as an instance, but it is a trial; a judge's quip from the bench gets the gallery chuckling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the reporters' note for the public gallery chuckling during a trial.

clue.text: Tries to get right into Cornish resort

indicators.note: into says the letter for right is placed inside the name of the resort

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to reach the correct seaside town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts, to attempt hard.

clue.text: Poe's tale of what bit the forty-niner?

explanation.surface: An Edgar Allan Poe story about a gold-rush prospector being bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: A forty-niner was a prospector in the 1849 California gold rush, so the bug that bit him was gold fever.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gold-Bug is a Poe short story about treasure hunting; a gold bug is also the fever for gold that gripped prospectors.

clue.text: Our crusty aristocracy ?

parts.note: crusty points to the phrase upper crust, and the expression meant is an old name for the topmost social set

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered nobles complain about the state of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusty' looks like grumpy, but it means upper-crust, the top layer of society.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is short for the upper ten thousand, the wealthiest and most aristocratic families.

clue.text: Sort of port fly-by-night ?

parts.note: a kind of port wine supplies the colour word, and a fly-by-night is a creature active after dark

explanation.surface: A dodgy kind of harbour operator.
explanation.walkthrough: Tawny is a style of port; a fly-by-night here is a nocturnal bird, not a shady trader.
explanation.definitionFit: This brown nocturnal bird shares its colour name with a style of aged port.

clue.text: Charming warning of evil around about

indicators.note: around says the word for evil wraps the word for about

parts.note: sin is evil or wrongdoing
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A delightful caution against wickedness on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a warning hooter, and the Sirens of myth charmed sailors with song.

clue.text: Wrong job for 2

parts.note: 2 is the misfit of the proverb, and the job it cannot fill is the opening it does not fit

explanation.surface: An unsuitable position for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 2 is SQUARE PEG; the proverb puts a misfit as a square peg in this.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is a square peg in this, the opening of the wrong shape.

clue.text: " and pie-crust are made to be broken" (Swift)

definitions.text: " and pie-crust are made to be broken" (Swift)

parts.words: " and pie-crust are made to be broken" (Swift)
parts.note: the gap is filled by the word Swift paired with fragile pastry, things given only to be broken

explanation.surface: A Swift saying about pastry that crumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift wrote that these and pie-crust are made to be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledges, like flaky pastry, are proverbially easy to break.

clue.text: Sort of elephant Hamlet accused himself of being?

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince calls himself a kind of pachyderm.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's soliloquy begins 'O, what a rogue and peasant slave am I!'
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue elephant lives apart from the herd and is dangerous; Hamlet calls himself a scoundrel in his soliloquy.

clue.text: Follow round it in succession

indicators.note: round says the word for follow is placed about the word it

parts.note: to ensue is to follow

explanation.surface: Go after it around in a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: En suite means forming a set or following on as part of a series.

clue.text: Strikes in order to keep company

explanation.surface: Workers down tools so that they can spend time together.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who go on strike leave the workplace; a courting couple who see each other regularly are said to do this together.

clue.text: Loud-speaker, from Shooter's Hill ?

parts.note: a Sten is a gun, a shooter
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A public-address system on Shooter's Hill, in south-east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooter's Hill reads as a London place name, but splits into STEN (a gun) and TOR (a hill).
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was the herald in the Iliad with the voice of fifty men, so a stentor is anyone very loud.

clue.text: Gives out a store of eloquence

definitions.text: Gives out a store of eloquence

parts.words: Gives out a store of eloquence
parts.note: said ironically: the speaker pours out a stream of words that are fluent but empty

explanation.surface: Someone dispenses a supply of fine oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds admiring, but it is ironic: the eloquence is idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to chatter on foolishly and at length.

clue.text: Wine varies my meals

indicators.note: varies says the letters of the two following words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: The choice of drink changes with each dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmsey is a sweet fortified Madeira wine.

clue.text: Slow movement of many an old ship

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, standing for many
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Many an ancient vessel moves slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a slow, broad section of a piece of music.

clue.text: Fast reactor down on the farm?

explanation.surface: A speedy response heard about on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A fast breeder is a kind of nuclear reactor; on a farm a breeder raises livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast breeder is a nuclear reactor making more fuel than it uses; a breeder also raises animals for stock.

clue.text: Where there'd be one artist in Mozambique

parts.note: be is the verb in there'd be
I is the Roman numeral one
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A place in Mozambique would have a single painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where ... in Mozambique' is the definition, with the wordplay set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beira is a port city in Mozambique, the place asked for.

clue.text: Means of restraining violence, keeping people under canvas

definitions.text: Means of restraining violence, keeping people under canvas

parts.words: Means of restraining violence, keeping people under canvas
parts.note: under canvas suggests camping, but the canvas is the stout cloth of a restraining garment for violent patients

explanation.surface: Campers are kept in tents to stop them fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' usually means camping, but here it is a canvas garment that holds the arms of a violent person.
explanation.definitionFit: This old name for a straitjacket describes a canvas garment binding a violent person's arms.

clue.text: Disturbed rest all round approved by Dracula's author!

indicators.note: all round says the rearranged letters surround the word for approved
disturbed says the letters of rest are thrown out of order

parts.note: OK means approved

explanation.surface: Someone's sleep is broken, and an author of horror gives his approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' turns REST into STER, and 'all round' puts it around OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker wrote the vampire novel Dracula.

clue.text: Hounds those on the run down

explanation.surface: Dogs chase people who are fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: Harriers are hounds for hunting hares; cross-country running clubs, out on the downs, also take the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriers are hare-hunting dogs, and also cross-country runners racing over the downs.
